findings.source_quote: ὃν ἰδία ὑμῖν ἑκάστοτε οὐ παύσομαι ἐκτιθέμενος κεφαλαιωδῶς
findings.english_quote: which I will not cease setting out for you separately, from time to time, in outline
findings.issue: ἑκάστοτε means “on each occasion” or “each time.” “From time to time” weakens this to occasional repetition.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace “from time to time” with “on each occasion”: “which I will not cease setting out for you separately, on each occasion, in outline.”

findings.source_quote: τὴν ἁμαρτίαν εἰς ἐκεῖνον ἀναφερομένην ἔχει, οὗπερ καθ᾽ ὁμοίωσιν ἡ εἰκὼν ἐτύγχανεν οὖσα.
findings.english_quote: has the sin charged to the one whose likeness the image happened to bear.
findings.issue: “Charged to” makes the represented person appear to bear the offender’s guilt. In this argument, εἰς ἐκεῖνον ἀναφερομένην describes the offense as reaching or being directed against the person represented by the insulted image, not as transferring culpability to that person.
findings.suggested_revision: Use wording that preserves the direction of the offense, such as “commits a sin against the one whose likeness the image happened to bear.”

findings.source_quote: ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς αὐτοῦ μαθηταῖς ὡς πρὸς ἀδελφοὺς ἔχοντας τὰ ὅμοια ποιεῖν ἐδίδασκεν.
findings.english_quote: but also taught his disciples that they must do the same toward brothers.
findings.issue: The draft does not explicitly preserve the brother-comparison and disposition expressed by ὡς πρὸς ἀδελφοὺς ἔχοντας. “Toward brothers” reads as a recipient category rather than conduct “as toward brothers.” The note’s appeal to an obligation sense of ἔχειν does not adequately account for this wording, especially alongside the repeated father-comparisons. The printed four-dot lacuna is correctly retained and disclosed; it is not the reason for revision.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare and freshly review a rendering such as “but also taught his disciples to do the same, with the disposition one has toward brothers.” Explain the relational construction ἔχειν πρός in the note. If an obligation interpretation is retained as an alternative, explain how it accounts for ὡς without suppressing the comparison.
